system_description.narrative_title: Russian escalation and geopolitical spillover across Europe and beyond
system_description.narrative_summary: A concentrated escalation of Russian military strikes, technology transfers, and hybrid operations against Ukraine is generating broader geopolitical spillovers that stress European security, test NATO deterrence, and deepen global alignments with Moscow. The system is open: kinetic attacks, information operations, economic ties and energy/commodity flows interact with alliance politics, domestic politics in EU states, arms transfers, and proxy partnerships (e.g., North Korea, Sahel), producing feedbacks such as Western aid decisions, sanctions, and regional militarisation.
system_description.scope: Military operations and strategic decisions by Russia and Ukraine (strikes, new weapons, drone/jet-drone tech), NATO/EU political and military responses (visits, troop movements, aid, sanctions), Russia's external partnerships and proxy influence (North Korea, Sahel juntas), hybrid warfare across Europe (infrastructure strikes, threats to NATO territories), and economic/energy linkages (oil deals, corporate ties) that mediate pressure and incentives.
system_description.super_system: The Euro-Atlantic security environment and the wider international geopolitical-economic order
adjacent_subsystems: EU political economy and budget/sanctions decision-making
NATO military posture, deterrence and force deployment in Europe
Arms proliferation, technology transfer and proxy networks (e.g., Russia–North Korea; Sahel)
Energy and commodity markets (oil deals, trade ties, corporate Russia links)

variables.name: Kinetic strike intensity
variables.description: The overall rate, scale and destructiveness of direct kinetic attacks (air, missile, artillery, large drones) across the theatre.

variables.name: Weapon-technology diffusion
variables.description: The speed and breadth with which weapons designs, delivery systems and enabling technologies spread between actors and proxies.

variables.name: Hybrid attack activity
variables.description: The frequency and geographic reach of non-kinetic and ambiguous operations such as cyber intrusions, sabotage, electoral influence and small-drone strikes.

variables.name: Alliance deterrence cohesion
variables.description: The perceived unity, policy alignment and credibility of collective defence commitments among security partners.

variables.name: Force deployment density
variables.description: The concentration and forward posture of military forces and assets positioned in or near contested regions.

variables.name: Military aid flows
variables.description: The volume, tempo and composition of transfers of weapons, equipment, logistics and finance to combatants and partners.

variables.name: Sanctions pressure
variables.description: The intensity, scope and enforcement rigor of economic, financial and trade restrictions applied across actors.

variables.name: Energy trade interdependence
variables.description: The depth and asymmetry of energy and key commodity trade links that create economic leverage or vulnerability between actors.

variables.name: Domestic political stability
variables.description: The resilience or fragility of domestic political systems, including government durability and protest/polarisation dynamics.

variables.name: Public war support
variables.description: Aggregate popular support, fatigue or opposition within societies toward continued military engagement and external aid.

variables.name: Proxy partnership strength
variables.description: The depth, institutionalisation and resource-exchange capacity of indirect partnerships and proxy networks.

variables.name: Information operation intensity
variables.description: The scale, sophistication and reach of coordinated messaging, disinformation and influence campaigns across media channels.

variables.name: Critical infrastructure vulnerability
variables.description: The exposure and fragility of civilian and logistical infrastructure (transport, energy, communications) to disruption or attack.

variables.name: Financial market volatility
variables.description: Cross-border financial stress measured by asset price swings, capital flight, liquidity squeezes and transaction interruptions.

variables.name: Arms stockpile
variables.description: The available inventories of munitions, spare parts and deployable weapons that determine sustainment of military operations.

variables.name: Nuclear rhetoric intensity
variables.description: The frequency, escalation and coercive severity of declaratory nuclear or extreme-escala­tion threats and messaging.

catalysts.title: Escalation: intensifying strikes on Kyiv/infrastructure
catalysts.description: Sustained Russian campaign to increase missile, drone and air strikes against Kyiv and critical Ukrainian infrastructure in near term.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Russia to intensify strikes on Ukraine', 'Russia strikes Kyiv as Germany’s Merz visits', 'Russia ramps up attacks on Kyiv infrastructure.'

catalysts.title: Ukraine targets Russian refineries
catalysts.description: Ukrainian leadership signals and likely conducts strikes on Russian energy/refinery infrastructure in retaliation, increasing cross-border energy targeting.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Ukraine will hit Russian refineries in response to Moscow's "new doctrine" of airstrikes, Zelenskiy says.'

catalysts.title: Russia–North Korea tech exchanges and missile drills
catalysts.description: Evidence of Russian sharing of jet-drone technology and concurrent North Korean missile/hypersonic drills increases technology transfer and proliferation risk.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Ukraine believes Russia shared jet-drone technology with North Korea' and 'North Korea ... intermediate-range strategic missile drill' / 'hypersonic missile drill.'

catalysts.title: Expansion of hybrid attacks in Europe
catalysts.description: Rise in ambiguous/deniable operations — drones, sabotage, information campaigns and strikes on civilian nodes — across EU/Nato space.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Russia puts lives at risk across Europe with hybrid attacks, Kallas says', 'Lithuania closed Vilnius airport, scrambled NATO jets due to suspected drone', 'Sahel juntas launch TV channel with Russian backing.'

catalysts.title: NATO/EU forward deployments and aid posture shift
catalysts.description: Member states reposition troops (e.g., Estonia) and increase aid/forward posture in response to threats, raising force density and sustainment flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Estonia shifts troops closer to Russia', 'Estonia moves troops closer to Russian border', 'Merz unveils fresh military aid in Kyiv.'

catalysts.title: EU votes and funding decisions for Ukraine/Moldova
catalysts.description: Near-term EU institutional decisions (vetos, budget ultimatums, subsidy access) that will unlock or constrain funding and integration for Ukraine/Moldova.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Hungary set to drop veto on Ukraine and Moldova EU bid progress', 'Germany issues EU budget ultimatum', 'EU pushes Ukraine for further reforms to unlock funding.'

catalysts.title: US–Russia negotiations linked to oil/deals
catalysts.description: Ongoing talks reportedly linking Ukraine negotiations to a large oil deal, which could alter sanctions enforcement and energy ties if concluded.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US-Russia talks on Ukraine involve multi-billion dollar oil deal, NYT reports.'

catalysts.title: Escalatory rhetoric; abandonment of rules of war
catalysts.description: Russian leadership directives to abandon rules of war and extreme threats (including versus NATO/Kaliningrad) increase coercive messaging and potential escalatory action.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Putin has told military leaders to abandon rules of war, Zelenskyy says', 'Russia makes extreme threats against Nato countries over Kaliningrad.'
